Nadia (ops): RCA published for the late-night degraded-serving incident: https://redwood.company/rca/2750011111 Please read before tomorrow's sync. :memo:
Nadia (ops): Short gist: 18m window, intermittent 504s for Dedicated customers due to a scaler/healthcheck interplay that caused some replicas to be removed while warm caches were still being used. Root cause: healthcheck threshold mismatch + flaky probe during rolling updates.
Nadia (ops): Impact: small percentage of requests (~2.4%) saw degraded tail latency; no auth or data leak. Customers with strict SLAs may have seen alerts.
Nadia (ops): Key actions and owners (from RCA):
- A1 (P0): Strict healthcheck alignment and deploy-time probe freeze 14: owner Tom (infra) 14 target: 48h
- A2 (P1): Canary playbook to ensure cache-warm handoff on scale events 14: owner Priya (sre) 14 target: 7 days
- A3 (P1): Short-term bump of probe timeout for older GPU SKUs during rolling updates 14: owner Evan (eng) 14 target: today, if safe
- A4 (P2): Runbook for owner rotation and on-call handoffs during rollouts 14: owner Marco (product) 14 target: 2 sprints
Nadia (ops): We're scheduling a 30m walkthrough tomorrow 09:00 PST to go over the canary playbook and backport decision tree. Invite sent to involved owners. If you can't make it, please add notes to the incident card.
Tom (infra): I'm taking A1. I have a branch that centralizes healthcheck config and ties it to rollout strategy. Will try to get a hotfix into the infra-stable channel after a quick smoke.
Tom (infra): core check we used to find bad probes: ```yaml
# simplified probe dump
- name: health
  path: /healthz
  timeout: 1s # problematic
  success_threshold: 1
  failure_threshold: 3
```
Priya (sre): I'll own the canary playbook. Planning: steady ramp, pre-warm cache step, and a 5m validation window before scale-down. Draft checklist attached to the incident card.
Priya (sre): proposal for playbook steps: 1) route 1% traffic to canary 2) validate tail-latency & error-rate 3) run cache-warm job 4) increase to 10% etc.
Evan (eng): I can do the probe timeout bump (A3) if Tom signs off on safety for production; will add a config flag so we can revert quickly.
Marco (product): For A4 I'll make the runbook include explicit owner rotation on code freeze days and a small template for handoff notes. Also will add a single-sentence customer note template for Support.
Ruth (support): I'll coordinate the outbound customer notes post-fix. Can we have a short blurb that explains mitigation and the timeline? I can draft and loop in legal.
Nadia (ops): Agreed. Please keep the language: clear, non-technical, and include workaround (restart client connections or retry after 30s).
oncall-bot: Incident 2024-04-02 23:18 UTC 14 annotated: assigned Priya (sre) as lead for canary-playbook
Lina (ceo): Thanks for the quick RCA and clear owners. Prioritize the hotfix and playbook; customers first. Happy to join the 09:00 PST call if useful. :heart:
Tom (infra): Quick note on backports: we should avoid backporting to very old dedicated clusters unless the owner signs off; differences in agent versions can cause probe semantics to diverge. I'll add a short decision tree to the PR.
Priya (sre): I'll run the first manual canary run in staging tonight and post results here. If we see any anomalies we'll pause rollout.
Evan (eng): PR for probe timeout bump: will link when ready.
Nadia (ops): Please update the incident board and link PRs/test artifacts before the 09:00 PST sync. We'll close the loop there and post summary notes after.
Marco (product): Adding postmortem follow-up checkpoint: 2-week review for regression tests and automation improvements.
Nadia (ops): Thanks team. Closing thread for now; will reopen after the sync with the decision and next steps. :white_check_mark:
